state.decided: J42_autostart_scope autostart_hide_duplicates p=0.98 (jev-1.13.0): hyprland-session.target Wants=xdg-desktop-autostart.target, so XDG login items start at login as on every desktop; nm-applet (duplicates the shell's network panel) and geoclue-demo-agent (Weather starts it on demand since b63a85283) are hidden with Hidden=true user overrides.
state.kdeconnect_found: J42's worker found a third system login item the decision did not cover: /etc/xdg/autostart/org.kde.kdeconnect.daemon.desktop (Exec=/usr/bin/kdeconnectd, no OnlyShowIn or NotShowIn). After J42, kdeconnectd starts at every login on a fresh install.
state.kdeconnect_in_koompi: kdeconnect is a KOOMPI default app (koompi-apps PKGBUILD:100, debian and fedora app lists). KOOMPI's firewall profile opens 1714-1764 tcp+udp for it by default (installer post_install: ufw allow KOOMPI-KDEConnect), and koompi-remotedesktop-portal carries an allowlist so KDE Connect's Remote Input (phone as touchpad and keyboard) works on Hyprland. The shell itself has no KDE Connect UI.
state.history: Docs dropped in b6a9b83fd recorded: 'KDE Connect was already removed from required KOOMPI core session startup' (KOOMPI's own exec of kdeconnect-indicator) and 'KDE/GNOME desktop infrastructure is not a required part of the core session'. The founder's seat hides the login item with a Hidden=true copy (2026-07-21, comment 'Disabled for KOOMPI core session; launch KDE Connect manually if needed').

state.cost_measured: On the founder's seat now: Pss 5.3 MB resident plus 9.6 MB in swap (SwapPss). While running it listens on 1714-1764 and announces the PC on the LAN.
state.platforms: macOS keeps its phone link (Continuity, Handoff, AirDrop) on at all times. Plasma starts kdeconnectd at login through this same login item. Windows starts Phone Link at login.

J42_kdeconnect_login.instructions: After J42, kdeconnectd's own login item starts it at every login on a fresh install. What should KOOMPI ship?

criteria.leave_autostart: Ship nothing; the daemon's login item runs, as on Plasma. Strongest case: KDE Connect is a default app whose value is a phone that reaches the PC at any time (send files, clipboard, notifications, Remote Input), KOOMPI already opens its firewall ports, and login items now work like macOS Login Items; the earlier removal was KOOMPI's own exec of the indicator, not the app's login item. Cost: a LAN-visible daemon at every login on every machine, including ones that never pair a phone (5.3 MB resident and 9.6 MB swap measured).
criteria.hide_kdeconnect: Ship a third Hidden=true override, like nm-applet and geoclue. Strongest case: keeps the earlier line that KDE infrastructure is not part of the core session and matches the founder's own seat; nothing listens on the LAN until KDE Connect is opened. Cost: a paired phone cannot reach the PC until the user opens KDE Connect in that session, while the firewall keeps its ports open for a daemon that usually is not running.
